profile.reading:
CloudHQ LC14 sits at 22131 Loudoun County Parkway, Ashburn, Virginia, one of fourteen numbered buildings on CloudHQ's LC Campus, which the company's own current campus page places directly off Loudoun County Parkway "in the heart of Ashburn," describing the site as sitting amid "the densest concentration of fiber in the world." A third-party data center aggregator separately reports 108 megawatts specifically for LC14, a figure this profile notes as unconfirmed by the operator rather than adopting as fact. CloudHQ states the full LC Campus totals roughly 8.5 million square feet and 1,256 megawatts of total critical IT load across its fourteen data centers, with 756 megawatts currently available, a campus-wide total not broken out by individual building. CloudHQ was founded in 2016 by Hossein Fateh, who also founded QTS Realty Trust and, per CloudHQ's own materials, was the first person in the United States to obtain an IRS ruling allowing data center income to qualify for real estate investment trust tax treatment. CloudHQ is privately held through the Fateh Family Office, with regional headquarters in Washington DC, London, and Singapore, and states a company-wide net-zero emissions target by 2040, along with generator fuel supplied by HVO biodiesel "wherever it is reliably available." CloudHQ does not name a power utility for the LC Campus on its current site; Dominion Energy is the dominant electric utility across Loudoun County as a matter of public record.

Loudoun County's Ashburn corridor is the largest concentration of data center capacity in the world, hosting dozens of competing hyperscale and colocation operators within a few miles of CloudHQ's LC Campus. CloudHQ's global portfolio spans 23 campuses and more than 30 million square feet across six countries, with more than 1,380 megawatts of critical IT load already contracted company-wide and over 6,000 megawatts of further expansion potential, figures CloudHQ discloses on its own homepage alongside a stated 5.2-gigawatt global data center inventory.

Facility specific seeding pass 2026-09-02, batch 38 (CloudHQ VA missing-address campaign): preferred a distinguishing DataCenterMap address over a Baxtel figure shared with a neighboring row, refreshed company history from the operators own about and founder pages, flagged a second CloudHQ name collision on Wikipedia not present in a prior sessions notes. research_status remains complete.

[process narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] CloudHQ, the data center operator, was established in 2016 by Hossein Fateh, per the operators own current about page (cloudhq.com/about/) fetched fresh this session. Fateh previously served as CEO and co-founder of DuPont Fabros Technology, a data center company that sold for 7.8 billion dollars in 2017, and has built and operated more than 700 MW of data center capacity across his career, per CloudHQs own founder page (cloudhq.com/learn-about-our-founder/), also fetched fresh this session. CloudHQ operates as part of the Fateh Family Office, alongside affiliated companies CloudCapital, WindHQ, and Dalian Development, per the operators own about page. The company maintains three regional headquarters, a global headquarters in Washington DC, an EMEA headquarters in London, and an APAC headquarters in Singapore. Per the operators own current about page, CloudHQ now describes 23 global campuses, more than 1,380 MW of contracted critical IT load with more than 6,000 MW of expansion potential, more than 30 million square feet of global data center portfolio, and more than 330 employees. A prior research pass on these rows had already flagged that the domain cloudhq.net resolves to an unrelated Google Workspace and Gmail backup software company, not this data center operator, and correctly redirected to cloudhq.com. This session found a second, separate name collision worth flagging for a future researcher: the Wikipedia article at en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CloudHQ describes yet another different, unrelated company, a cloud data synchronization tool for Google Workspace founded in 2011 by Senad Dizdar and based in San Francisco, not this Ashburn and Manassas Virginia data center operator founded by Hossein Fateh. That Wikipedia article was checked this session and found not to apply, so it is not used or cited as a source here, and no Wikipedia sourced company history is included in this reading. This specific row, LC14, has conflicting aggregator sourcing. Baxtels own dedicated LC14 page gives 22141 Loudoun County Pkwy, Ashburn, the identical figure Baxtel separately assigns to neighboring LC13, so it does not distinguish this row from LC13. DataCenterMaps specs page for LC14 instead gives a distinct 22131 Loudoun County Pkwy, Ashburn, VA 20147, ten digits off from Baxtels figure but at least not colliding with LC13. Because the DataCenterMap figure is distinguishing, it is preferred here, with Baxtels competing, shared figure flagged rather than silently dropped.

reading.body:
CloudHQ LC14 is one building in a fourteen-building campus totaling 1,256 megawatts of critical IT load, with 756 megawatts currently available for new tenants. A third-party aggregator reports 108 megawatts for this specific building, a figure the operator has not confirmed. The campus sits in Ashburn, Virginia, directly off Loudoun County Parkway, in what CloudHQ describes as the densest concentration of fiber in the world.

The LC Campus occupies roughly 8.5 million square feet across Ashburn's corridor, which is the largest concentration of data center capacity globally and hosts dozens of competing operators within a few miles. Virginia as a state shows 326 mapped data center facilities with only 23 publishing power figures to this site; the entire CloudHQ LC Campus ranks 24th by published megawatts across Virginia, with a total of 1,256 megawatts representing about 91 percent of the 1,375 megawatts of published capacity the state reports. The operator does not publish the specific power utility serving this site.

CloudHQ states a global portfolio of 23 campuses across six countries with over 1,380 megawatts of contracted critical IT load and more than 6,000 megawatts of expansion potential, suggesting the Ashburn campus is material to the company's capacity. The Ashburn location's access to dense fiber, sitting amid a global hyperscale hub, means tenants placing accelerators here connect directly to the densest network routes in North America. Whether the campus can grow depends on grid availability, which the operator does not disclose.
